notes: largest nationally distributed Brazilian DENV serology; 16,235 randomised of whom 15,605 had known baseline VRNT60 serostatus; 8,050 seropositive. READ seroprev_pct AND THE COUNTS DIFFERENTLY: the paper prints seropositive percentages whose denominator includes unknown-serostatus participants, while n_tested here is seropositive+seronegative only. So seroprev_pct does NOT equal n_positive/n_tested for this study or any of its strata rows. Measured across all 8 extracted Table 2 rows the printed value sits between 0.17pp and 4.40pp BELOW the count fraction (smallest: South 28/477=5.87% vs 5.7% printed; largest: 18-59y 4060/5694=71.30% vs 66.9% printed; overall 8050/15605=51.59% vs 49.6% printed). The gap is not a fixed offset and is not bounded by 3pp - compute it per row rather than assuming a range. This is by design, not an error; do not "fix" it. SUPERSEDED FIGURES - DO NOT USE: registry v0.1-v0.9 recorded 2-6y 19.0%, 18-59y 73.1% and South region 8.2% for this study. Those were not printed values at all - they were derived as 100 minus %seronegative, a different and incorrect calculation. The printed seropositive figures for those three strata are 17.3%, 66.9% and 5.7% (corrected rows BR006-A1/A3/R1 in the strata file). Note 73.1 vs 66.9 is the size of that derivation ERROR, NOT a printed-vs-count offset - the two quantities must not be compared. ASSAY: VRNT60 against DENV-1..4, so "seropositive" means any-serotype neutralising titre above LOD, not a serotype-specific prevalence. 100% prior yellow fever vaccination by design.
